key_insight: SPICE-Q is a SPICE-like co-optimization framework that links superconducting qubit design stages into one traceable pipeline from process rules to quantum performance.
engineering_relevance: It gives quantum hardware teams a practical workflow for integrating layout, EM simulation, circuit quantization, noise analysis, fabrication, and cryogenic test to improve scalability and yield.
method: Unifies existing tools (HFSS, Qiskit Metal, pyEPR, SQcircuit, SQuADDS, scqubits, QuTiP) through standardized interfaces.
Maps process/PDK constraints to geometry, EM modes, circuit parameters, Hamiltonians, and device metrics.
Adds statistical parameter models, model cards, version governance, and closed-loop calibration from fab and cryogenic data.
evidence_signal: The abstract is a framework proposal and synthesis of the design-to-test workflow, not a results paper with reported experimental benchmarks or quantitative evaluation.
watch_item: A major implementation challenge is ensuring consistent models and data exchange across heterogeneous tools while capturing junction variability, parasitics, and wafer-scale process statistics accurately.
paper_title: SPICE-Q and Large-Scale Quantum Chip Production
